rv.q: As a piece of writing, “Routes” is distant itself: it has a clinical kind of detachment that sometimes seems at odds with the urgency of the subject matter.
But the brief and sometimes rushed scenes, and an abrupt ending, give the work a feeling of irresolution.
But with three loosely connected storylines taking place concurrently, the tale is being told in a somewhat confusing manner that detracts from its very disturbing message...

cn.t: Well-intentioned drama about immigration and deportation proves timely and thought-provoking but suffers from a purposefully disjointed, murky script that undermines its relevant themes about refugees seeking home.
